question: Nico controls Analia's [Bane Alley Blackguard] enchanted with their [Corrupted Conscience]. Analia casts their own [Lay Claim], targeting Nico's Corrupted Conscience. After it resolves, who controls the Bane Alley Blackguard? Who controls the Corrupted Conscience?
answer:
Analia ends up controlling both. Once Analia's Lay Claim resolves and enchants Nico's Corrupted Conscience, Analia controls Corrupted Conscience, and because Corrupted Conscience reads "You control enchanted creature," its "you" now means Analia — so Analia also takes control of Bane Alley Blackguard (which Analia owns anyway).

Why:
- An Aura is a permanent, and Lay Claim's enchant ability is "enchant permanent," so it can legally be attached to Corrupted Conscience. An Aura's controller is tracked separately from the controller of what it enchants [303.4e], so Corrupted Conscience being attached to Bane Alley Blackguard doesn't stop a separate effect from changing who controls Corrupted Conscience itself.
- Control-changing effects are all applied in layer 2 [613.1b]. Lay Claim's effect makes Analia the controller of Corrupted Conscience; Corrupted Conscience's own effect then grants control of the enchanted creature to whoever currently controls Corrupted Conscience. That's Analia, so Bane Alley Blackguard changes from Nico's control to Analia's control.
- The Lay Claim ruling confirms the principle: an Aura's effect that refers to "you" affects the Aura's controller, not some other player [Lay Claim ruling #0].
- Nico is left controlling nothing here; Bane Alley Blackguard's default controller (the player under whose control it entered) is unchanged as a default [110.2], but the layer-2 effects determine actual control, and both now point to Analia.

If Nico's Corrupted Conscience had granted anything that triggers on losing control of a permanent, note that such abilities "look back in time" [603.10d] — but neither Bane Alley Blackguard nor Corrupted Conscience as printed has such a trigger, so nothing triggers.

Multiplayer: the answer is the same at any table size. No third player gains anything, since only the controllers of Lay Claim and Corrupted Conscience matter. (If a player later leaves a multiplayer game, control effects they own end and can send objects back or to exile [800.4a, 800.4c], but that's not in play here.)

Otherwise, the effect is considered to be independent of the other effect.

If a dependency exists, it will override the timestamp system. An effect dependent on one or more other effects waits to apply until just after all of those effects have been applied. If multiple dependent effects would apply simultaneously in this way, they’re applied in timestamp order relative to each other. If several dependent effects form a dependency loop, then this rule is ignored and the effects in the dependency loop are applied in timestamp order.

However, some triggered abilities are exceptions to this rule; the game “looks back in time” to determine if those abilities trigger, using the existence of those abilities and the appearance of objects immediately prior to the event. The list of exceptions is as follows: Abilities that trigger when a player loses control of an object or when a player’s opponent gains control of an object from that player look back in time.

Then, if that player controlled any objects on the stack not represented by cards, those objects cease to exist. Then, if there are any objects still controlled by that player, those objects are exiled. This is not a state-based action. It happens as soon as the player leaves the game. If the player who left the game had priority at the time they left, priority passes to the next player in turn order who’s still in the game. Alex casts Mind Control, an Aura that reads, “You control enchanted creature,” on Bianca’s Assault Griffin. If Alex leaves the game, so does Mind Control, and Assault Griffin reverts to Bianca’s control. If, instead, Bianca leaves the game, so does Assault Griffin, and Mind Control is put into Alex’s graveyard. Alex casts Act of Treason, which reads, in part, “Gain control of target creature until end of turn,” targeting Bianca’s Runeclaw Bears. If Alex leaves the game, Act of Treason’s change-of-control effect ends and Runeclaw Bears reverts to Bianca’s control. Alex casts Bribery, which reads, “Search target opponent’s library for a creature card and put that card onto the battlefield under your control. Then that player shuffles their library,” targeting Bianca. Alex puts Serra Angel onto the battlefield from Bianca’s library. If Bianca leaves the game, Serra Angel also leaves the game. If, instead, Alex leaves the game, Serra Angel is exiled. Alex controls Genesis Chamber, which reads, “Whenever a nontoken creature enters, if Genesis Chamber is untapped, that creature’s controller creates a 1/1 colorless Myr artifact creature token.” If Alex leaves the game, all such Myr tokens that entered the battlefield under Alex’s control leave the game, and all such Myr tokens that entered the battlefield under any other player’s control remain in the game.
cited_text.800.4c: Unlike two-player games, multiplayer games can continue after one or more players have left the game. If an effect that gives a player still in the game control of an object ends, there is no other effect giving control of that object to another player in the game, and the player who controlled that object by default has left the game, the object is exiled. This is not a state-based action. It happens as soon as the control-changing effect ends.

answer_gold: Analia controls both permanents. Out of the two auras, Corrupted Conscience has the earlier timestamp, and would normally be applied first. However, the effects from both auras apply in the same layer, applying the Lay Claim's effect would change how the Corrupted Conscience's effect is applied, and applying the Corrupted Conscience's effect would not change how the Lay Claim's effect is applied, so the Corrupted Conscience's effect is dependent on the Lay Claim's effect. The Lay Claim's effect applies first, giving Analia control of Corrupted Conscience, and then the Corrupted Conscience's effect applies, giving Analia control of Bane Alley Blackguard.

question: Alex activates [Inkmoth Nexus] to turn it into a creature and attacks Nadia with it. Nadia doesn't block it and then casts [Summoning Trap], putting [Melira, Sylvok Outcast] onto the battlefield. What happens during the combat damage step?
answer:
Direct answer: Melira, Sylvok Outcast strips infect from Inkmoth Nexus, so in the combat damage step Inkmoth Nexus deals 1 ordinary combat damage to Nadia — she loses 1 life and gets no poison counters.

Why:

1. Inkmoth Nexus's activated ability makes it a 1/1 Phyrexian Blinkmoth artifact creature with flying and infect until end of turn (Inkmoth Nexus card text). Infect means damage to a player becomes poison counters rather than life loss [702.90b], and damage to a creature becomes -1/-1 counters rather than marked damage [702.90c].

2. Melira, Sylvok Outcast says "Creatures your opponents control lose infect." Because Melira, Sylvok Outcast entered the battlefield after Inkmoth Nexus's animation ability resolved, Melira, Sylvok Outcast's effect has the later timestamp and wins, so Inkmoth Nexus loses infect [Melira, Sylvok Outcast ruling #1] [Melira, Sylvok Outcast ruling #3]. Melira, Sylvok Outcast does not undo the animation — Inkmoth Nexus is still an attacking 1/1 creature with flying.

3. In the combat damage step, Alex announces Inkmoth Nexus's damage assignment as a turn-based action [510.1] [703.4k], and that damage is then dealt immediately, with no priority in between [510.2] [703.4m]. Inkmoth Nexus deals damage equal to its power, 1 [120.2a]. With infect gone, that damage is processed into its normal result [120.3] [120.4b]: Nadia loses 1 life. Even if some other effect gave Inkmoth Nexus infect again, Melira, Sylvok Outcast's "You can't get poison counters" would stop the poison counters, though the damage would still be treated as having been dealt [Melira, Sylvok Outcast ruling #1].

Timing assumption: I'm assuming Nadia cast Summoning Trap during the declare blockers step (or an earlier point in combat), before the combat damage step began. That's the only workable window, since no player receives priority between damage assignment and damage being dealt [510.2]. If instead combat damage had already been dealt before Summoning Trap resolved, Nadia would already have taken 1 poison counter from the infect damage, and Melira, Sylvok Outcast arriving afterward would only prevent her from getting future poison counters — it doesn't remove counters she already has.

Player count: this works the same in a two-player game and at a multiplayer table. Melira, Sylvok Outcast removes infect from creatures controlled by all of Nadia's opponents, not just Alex, and "You can't get poison counters" protects only Nadia. Other players at the table are unaffected and can still be hit by infect damage from Inkmoth Nexus in later combats if it's animated again. Under the shared team turns multiplayer option, the attacking team assigns combat damage first and then the defending team assigns blocker damage [805.10f], but the outcome here is unchanged.

question: Nathaniel controls a [Melira, Sylvok Outcast]. Ari activates [Inkmoth Nexus] to turn it into a creature and attacks Nathaniel with it. Nathaniel doesn't block. What happens during the combat damage step?
answer:
Short answer: Inkmoth Nexus deals 1 combat damage to Nathaniel, and nothing happens as a result — Nathaniel loses no life and gets no poison counters.

Why:

1. Does the animated Inkmoth Nexus still have infect? Yes. Melira, Sylvok Outcast says "Creatures your opponents control lose infect," but Inkmoth Nexus's activated ability ("{1}: This land becomes a 1/1 Phyrexian Blinkmoth artifact creature with flying and infect until end of turn") is applied after Melira, Sylvok Outcast's effect in timestamp order, so the more recent effect wins and Inkmoth Nexus has infect. This is exactly the situation described in [Melira, Sylvok Outcast ruling #1], where a creature that gains infect after Melira, Sylvok Outcast is already on the battlefield keeps it. (I'm assuming the order stated in the question: Melira, Sylvok Outcast was already on the battlefield when Ari activated Inkmoth Nexus. If Inkmoth Nexus had been animated first and Melira, Sylvok Outcast entered afterward, Melira, Sylvok Outcast would strip infect and the 1 damage would simply make Nathaniel lose 1 life per [120.3a].)

2. The combat damage step: as it begins, Ari announces damage assignment — Inkmoth Nexus is unblocked and attacking Nathaniel, so it assigns its 1 damage to Nathaniel [703.4k], [510.1], [510.1b], [120.2a]. Immediately after, that damage is dealt simultaneously as a turn-based action that doesn't use the stack; no one gets priority in between [703.4m], [510.2], [120.4b].

3. Processing the damage into results: because the source, Inkmoth Nexus, has infect, the 1 damage does not cause Nathaniel to lose life; instead it would cause Ari to give Nathaniel 1 poison counter [120.3b], [702.90b], [702.90e]. But Melira, Sylvok Outcast says "You can't get poison counters," so Nathaniel gets none. That step of the sequence is where results are modified [120.4c], and then the (now empty) damage event occurs [120.4d]. Net effect on Nathaniel: zero life lost, zero poison counters.

4. Damage was still dealt. Per [Melira, Sylvok Outcast ruling #1], abilities that check whether damage was dealt (lifelink, "whenever this deals combat damage to a player" triggers, etc.) still see the 1 damage, so if Ari had such an effect it would still work.

Multiplayer note: in a game with more than two players, combat damage is assigned in APNAP order but the step otherwise works identically [802.5]. Melira, Sylvok Outcast only protects Nathaniel ("You can't get poison counters") and only strips infect from creatures Nathaniel's opponents control — so if Ari attacked a different player with Inkmoth Nexus, that player would take 1 poison counter normally.
